title: Microsoft Purview: information protection scanner data export for custom reporting
summary: The briefing accurately distinguishes the roadmap targets from the documented Custom Reporting preview. The scanner controls, administrator opt-in default, database behavior and licensing statements are supported by Microsoft's documentation.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes learning about scanned repositories and creating custom reports with the information protection scanner.
claims.quote: Learn about the state of your scanned repositories and create custom reports with the information protection scanner.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes storing labeling, classification and protection actions on scanned files in SQL tables as a foundation for custom reports.
claims.quote: Labeling, classification and protection actions on scanned files are stored in SQL tables that form a foundation to feed into custom reports.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; controls[2].note; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents Custom Reporting as a preview.
claims.quote: This article describes the Microsoft Purview Information Protection scanner Custom Reporting feature (preview).

claims.claim: Custom Reporting requires Microsoft Purview Information Protection client and scanner version 3.2.89.0 or later.
claims.quote: Custom Reporting is available with Microsoft Purview Information Protection client and scanner version 3.2.89.0 or later.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; controls[2].note; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Custom Reporting is off by default and requires administrator enablement, corresponding to admin-opt-in.
claims.quote: Scanner administrators can enable, disable, and configure Microsoft Purview Information Protection scanner features at the cluster level. | CustomReporting | Off | $true, $false |

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Custom Reporting stores reporting data in the scanner cluster database.
claims.quote: Custom Reporting gives scanner administrators the data they need in the scanner cluster database to build their own reports against scan results—including labeling, protection state, and matched sensitive information types (SITs).

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; controls[2].note
claims.claim: Reporting data starts populating on the next scan cycle after enablement.
claims.quote: Custom Reporting writes the additional reporting data to the scanner cluster database on the next scan cycle after the feature is enabled.

claims.claim: Custom Reporting adds reporting columns to dbo.ScannerFiles, with definitions documented on the feature page.
claims.quote: Additions to dbo.ScannerFiles ... Custom Reporting populates the following additional columns to capture file state and the delta between the current and previous scan:

claims.claim: The preview documents the new dbo.MatchedClassificationAction table and its columns.
claims.quote: dbo.MatchedClassificationAction is a new table that stores the matched sensitive information types per file per scan. Each row represents one matched SIT for a single file in a single scan session.

claims.claim: The preview documents the new dbo.ScannedFilesArchive table and its columns.
claims.quote: dbo.ScannedFilesArchive is a new table that stores a historical archive of files the scanner processed, with rows tied to the scan session that created them.

claims.claim: The scanner runs as a service on Windows Server.
claims.quote: This scanner runs as a service on Windows Server and lets you discover, classify, and protect files on the following data stores:

claims.claim: The scanner uses sensitivity labels configured in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: To classify and protect your files, the scanner uses sensitivity labels configured in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Completed-scan reports are stored on the scanner computer in %localappdata%\Microsoft\MSIP\Scanner\Reports.
claims.quote: When the scan is complete, review the reports stored in the %localappdata%\Microsoft\MSIP\Scanner\Reports directory.

claims.claim: The scanner produces .txt summary reports.
claims.quote: The .txt summary files include the time taken to scan, the number of scanned files, and how many files had a match for the information types.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The scanner's .csv reports contain more detail for each file.
claims.quote: The .csv files have more details for each file.

claims.claim: The admin portal displays information about the last scan only.
claims.quote: The admin portal displays information about the last scan only.

claims.claim: Results of previous scans are available in reports stored on the scanner computer.
claims.quote: If you need to see the results of previous scans, return to the reports that are stored on the scanner computer

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: SQL Server database permissions govern access to the reporting data stored in the scanner cluster database.
claims.quote: Database-level roles are database-wide in their permissions scope. ... Members of the db_datareader fixed database role can read all data from all user tables and views.

claims.claim: Members of db_datareader on the scanner database can read its reporting tables.
claims.quote: Members of the db_datareader fixed database role can read all data from all user tables and views. User objects can exist in any schema except sys and INFORMATION_SCHEMA.

claims.claim: The scanner report folder location or name cannot be changed.
claims.quote: The report folder location or name can't be changed. If you want to store reports in a different location, consider using a directory junction for the folder.

claims.claim: The scanner installation process grants db_owner on the scanner configuration database to the scanner service account.
claims.quote: The Sysadmin role enables the installation process to automatically create the scanner configuration database and grant the required db_owner role to the service account that runs the scanner.

claims.where: Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance; controls[0].note
claims.claim: Scanner configuration in the Microsoft Purview portal requires Compliance Administrator, Compliance Data Administrator, Security Administrator or Organization Management.
claims.quote: To configure your scanner in the Microsoft Purview portal: ... Sign in using one of the following roles: ... Compliance Administrator ... Compliance Data Administrator ... Security Administrator ... Organization Management

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft does not state whether an additional Microsoft Purview portal role is required specifically to enable Custom Reporting.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Purview scanner Custom Reporting feature control permissions roles Compliance Administrator. Read Custom Reporting, feature control, Set-ScannerConfiguration, scanner prerequisites and Purview permissions search results; none specifies an additional portal role for this switch.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes storing scanner action results, not introducing new actions.
claims.quote: Labeling, classification and protection actions on scanned files are stored in SQL tables that form a foundation to feed into custom reports.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The content scan job's Enforce setting controls enforcement of scanning and labeling according to policy.
claims.quote: -Enforce: Determines whether the content scan job enforces content scanning and labeling according to your policy.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Scanner upgrades include running Update-ScannerDatabase to update the scanner database.
claims.quote: Update the scanner database: On one scanner node, run the following command: ... Update-ScannerDatabase

claims.claim: Scanner installation or upgrade deploys the full Custom Reporting database schema.
claims.quote: Whether you're installing the scanner fresh or upgrading from any earlier version, the scanner deploys the full database schema (including the Custom Reporting tables and columns) on install or upgrade.

claims.claim: The added reporting columns and tables remain unpopulated until Custom Reporting is enabled.
claims.quote: Until Custom Reporting is enabled, the new columns and tables exist but aren't populated. Existing scanner functionality is unchanged.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft documents a sizing equation for the scanner configuration database.
claims.quote: The disk size for the scanner configuration database will vary for each deployment. Use the following equation as guidance: ... 100 KB + <file count> *(1000 + 4* <average file name length>)

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Enabling Custom Reporting significantly increases scanner cluster database storage.
claims.quote: When you turn on Custom Reporting, the scanner cluster database stores significantly more data:

claims.claim: Building reports against the scanner cluster database adds reads alongside scanner operations.
claims.quote: Building reports against the scanner cluster database also adds a read workload that runs alongside the scanner's operational reads and writes.

claims.claim: The scanner prerequisites require a License for information protection to provide classification, labeling or protection capabilities to its service account.
claims.quote: License for information protection | Required to provide file classification, labeling, or protection capabilities to the scanner service account.

claims.claim: The licensing model is included under the scanner's existing information protection licensing requirement.
claims.quote: License for information protection | Required to provide file classification, labeling, or protection capabilities to the scanner service account.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Licence; rationale: cost; Open questions
claims.claim: No separate license or plan specific to scanner Custom Reporting is published as of the run.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Purview scanner Custom Reporting license pricing meter charge. Read Custom Reporting, feature control, scanner prerequisites, Microsoft 365 Security and the Purview service description, searching the latter for scanner and Custom Reporting; no export-specific plan was found.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Meter; rationale: cost; Open questions
claims.claim: No meter, price or charge specific to the scanner export is documented as of the run.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Purview scanner Custom Reporting license pricing meter charge. Read Custom Reporting, feature control, scanner prerequisites, Purview service description and Purview billing models; none states a meter, price or charge for scanner Custom Reporting.

claims.claim: The scanner prerequisites link their licensing requirement to Microsoft's security and compliance licensing guidance.
claims.quote: For more information, see the Microsoft 365 guidance for security & compliance.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Indirect costs; Scope
claims.claim: The scanner requires an SQL Server instance to store its configuration data.
claims.quote: To store the scanner configuration data, use an SQL server with the following requirements: ... A local or remote instance.

claims.claim: SQL Server 2016 is the minimum version for the listed Enterprise, Standard and Express editions.
claims.quote: SQL Server 2016 is the minimum version for the following editions: ... SQL Server Enterprise ... SQL Server Standard ... SQL Server Express (recommended for test environments only)

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends SQL Server Express for test environments only.
claims.quote: SQL Server Express (recommended for test environments only)

claims.claim: The configuration database sizing example allocates 2 GB for 1 million files with an average file name length of 250 bytes.
claims.quote: For example, to scan 1 million files that have an average file name length of 250 bytes, allocate 2-GB disk space.

claims.claim: The scanner discovers, classifies and protects files in UNC network-share paths using SMB.
claims.quote: lets you discover, classify, and protect files on the following data stores: ... UNC paths for network shares that use the SMB or NFS (Preview) protocols.

claims.claim: NFS network-share scanning is documented as Preview.
claims.quote: UNC paths for network shares that use the SMB or NFS (Preview) protocols.

claims.claim: The scanner supports SharePoint Server document libraries.
claims.quote: SharePoint document libraries and folder for SharePoint Server (versions currently in extended support).

claims.claim: Scanner feature configuration is per scanner cluster.
claims.quote: Scanner features are configured once per scanner cluster. The settings are stored centrally in the shared scanner cluster database

claims.claim: All nodes in the cluster pick up feature configuration changes on the next scan cycle.
claims.quote: An administrator runs a configuration cmdlet once from any node in the cluster, and all nodes pick up the change on the next scan cycle.

claims.claim: Enforcement is configured in the Microsoft Purview portal at Settings > Information Protection > Information protection scanner > Content scan jobs > content scan job > Enforce sensitivity labeling policy.
claims.quote: Settings card > Information Protection > Information protection scanner. ... on the Content scan jobs tab, select a specific content scan job to edit it. ... From the Enforce sensitivity labeling policy section: Change the radio button to On

claims.claim: Set-ScannerContentScan -Enforce On in PurviewInformationProtection enables policy enforcement for a content scan job.
claims.quote: Module: PurviewInformationProtection Module ... -Enforce ... Determines whether the content scan job enforces content scanning and labeling according to your policy. ... Accepted values: On, Off

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: A scan is started in the Microsoft Purview portal at Settings > Information Protection > Information protection scanner > Content scan jobs > content scan job > Scan now.
claims.quote: On the Information protection scanner - Content scan jobs pane, select your content scan jobs, and then select the Scan now option.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Start-Scan in PurviewInformationProtection starts a one-time scan cycle.
claims.quote: Module: PurviewInformationProtection Module ... The Start-Scan cmdlet instructs the Microsoft Purview Information Protection scanner to immediately start a one-time scan cycle.

claims.claim: The Scan now option only appears once a content scan job is selected.
claims.quote: The Scan now option only appears once a content scan job is selected.

claims.claim: Start-Scan is ignored when the scanner schedule is Always.
claims.quote: If the scanner schedule is set to Always, this cmdlet is ignored.

claims.claim: No Microsoft Purview portal control for Custom Reporting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Purview scanner Custom Reporting enable portal UI Settings. Read Custom Reporting, scanner feature control, configure/install and manage pages. The feature is documented through PowerShell; no Custom Reporting portal path was found.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance controls table; summary; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Set-ScannerConfiguration -FeatureSettings @{CustomReporting=$true} in PurviewInformationProtection enables Custom Reporting.
claims.quote: Module: PurviewInformationProtection Module ... Set-ScannerConfiguration -FeatureSettings @{CustomReporting=$true} ... This command enables the Custom Reporting feature for the entire scanner cluster.

claims.claim: Setting CustomReporting to $false stops new reporting writes.
claims.quote: Set-ScannerConfiguration -FeatureSettings @{CustomReporting=$false} ... Disabling Custom Reporting stops new writes.

claims.claim: Disabling Custom Reporting retains existing reporting data.
claims.quote: Data already written to the reporting columns and tables isn't deleted, so the feature can be re-enabled later without data loss.

claims.claim: For features also configurable through the Microsoft Purview portal, portal-configured settings take precedence and prevent PowerShell updates.
claims.quote: When a feature is available in the portal and has been configured there, that portal-configured setting takes precedence and prevents updates from PowerShell.

claims.claim: Microsoft's initial scanner configuration instructions set Enforce sensitivity labeling policy to Off.
claims.quote: For this initial configuration, configure the following settings ... Sensitivity policy ... Enforce sensitivity labeling policy: Select Off

claims.claim: Start-Scan requires the scanner service to be started.
claims.quote: The scanner service must be started already and the scanner schedule must be configured for a manual schedule.

claims.claim: Start-Scan requires the scanner schedule to be Manual.
claims.quote: The scanner service must be started already and the scanner schedule must be configured for a manual schedule.

claims.claim: The user account configuring the scanner requires db_owner for the scanner configuration database.
claims.quote: However, the user account that configures the scanner still requires the db_owner role for the scanner configuration database.

claims.where: controls[0].note; controls[1].note; Governance controls: explanatory prose
claims.claim: The Enforce and Scan now controls govern existing scan behavior, not the Custom Reporting export switch.
claims.quote: Existing scanner functionality is unchanged. ... Custom Reporting is turned on through admin-controlled feature configuration. ... Set-ScannerConfiguration -FeatureSettings @{CustomReporting=$true}

claims.claim: The roadmap item names no effect on end users.
claims.quote: Learn about the state of your scanned repositories and create custom reports with the information protection scanner. Labeling, classification and protection actions on scanned files are stored in SQL tables that form a foundation to feed into custom reports.
